title: Access Pathways: Role Lifecycle & Audit Timeline Prototype
creator: Ethan Brooks
description: Problem: Customers managing many workspaces tell us it's hard to understand who actually has access and how that access changed over time. Current audit logs are noisy and disconnected from role lifecycle (creation, delegation, policy changes, membership). Goal: Create a compact, scannable 'Access Pathways' UX that surfaces role assignments, delegation chains, and an event-driven timeline for access changes tied to workspaces and org-level policies. Deliver a high-fidelity Figma prototype + interaction spec and a lightweight handoff package for frontend engineers and PMs.
scope: Design flows for org-level and workspace-level views, timeline of role changes, role assignment detail panel, search+filter for principal/role/time, CSV export affordance. Include lightweight mobile/tablet responsive considerations. Out of scope: backend audit storage or RBAC enforcement changes; those are covered by ENG dependents.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype demonstrates primary flows: org-level summary -> workspace rollup -> single-role timeline -> actor detail
Design spec includes clear component states for collapsed/expanded timelines, event grouping, and compact role tiles
Filters for date range, role type (builtin/custom), principal type (user/service), and event type (grant/revoke/policy-change) are defined
Export action and contextual links to related console pages (role editor, membership) are specified
PM and Eng sign-off recorded and a prioritized front-end ticket list created for implementation
decisions: Use a condensed vertical timeline with event grouping by day and by actor to reduce noise (vs a table-first approach) - chosen for scannability
Show both direct assignments and policy-driven grants; denote policy grants with a gray badge and link to policy editor
Default view is org-rollup with workspace filters; user can drill into a specific workspace or role
Favor progressive disclosure: show summary counts and top actors, with 'expand' to reveal full event stream
Export includes contextual columns (actor, role, grant_type, source_policy, timestamp, reason) to aid audits
tradeoffs: Timeline UX increases client-side rendering complexity; tradeoff accepted to improve investigator speed for security teams
Decision to show policy-derived grants in the same timeline could confuse non-expert users; mitigated by clear badges and hover explanatory text
Inline search across event messages may be limited in MVP to indexed fields to avoid backend perf changes
